name: Consciousness Foundations
crownClaim: Conscious experience exists as a real phenomenon, though its relationship to physical processes remains an open and foundational question
instructions: Research each claim. Subjective experience is the most certain axiom (Descartes' cogito). Neural correlates have strong empirical support. The hard problem is genuinely unsolved. Focus evidence on neuroscience of consciousness, philosophy of mind, and psychophysics.

claims.claim: Subjective experience (qualia) exists: there is something it is like to be a conscious being
searchHints: Nagel what is it like to be a bat

claims.claim: Specific patterns of neural activity consistently correlate with specific conscious states
Systematic, lawful relationships exist between physical stimuli and conscious experience (psychophysics)
Explaining why and how physical processes give rise to subjective experience (the 'hard problem') remains unsolved
Conscious experience exists as a real phenomenon, though its relationship to physical processes remains an open and foundational question

alternatives.claim: Consciousness is an illusion; folk-psychological concepts like qualia will be eliminated by neuroscience
Consciousness is a fundamental feature of all matter, not an emergent property unique to brains
Mind and body are fundamentally different substances; neural correlates reflect interaction, not identity
